summary: AI observability tools provide visibility into how LLM applications behave in production by tracing requests, evaluating output quality, tracking token usage, and alerting on failures or regressions. As LLM features scale, per-trace and per-token costs can grow unpredictably, making observability essential for controlling spend, debugging complex agent workflows, and maintaining reliable, high-quality AI systems.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, LLM/chain/agent execution, token usage, latency, evaluation scores, and prompt performance (tightly integrated with LangChain but framework-agnostic).
features: Detailed step-by-step tracing of chains and agents
tools.pricing: Developer tier free up to 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month with overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces; Plus plan reported at roughly $264 per 100,000 traces. Enterprise custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph that need deep tracing, evaluation, and prompt iteration in one platform.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests via a proxy/gateway — costs, token usage, latency, caching, rate limits, and request/response logs across providers.
tools.pricing: Free tier available; usage-based pricing reported at ~$79 per 100,000 traces with 30 days of data retention; Pro and Enterprise tiers for higher volumes.
tools.best_for: Cost-conscious teams wanting fast, low-overhead monitoring and caching across multiple LLM providers.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM traces and evaluations via W&B Weave, plus ML experiment tracking, model performance, token usage, and quality metrics across the full ML/LLM lifecycle.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; Teams/Pro plans typically starting around $50 per user/month; Enterprise custom pricing with volume-based usage.
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams that need unified observability spanning traditional ML experiments and modern LLM applications.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production and pre-production LLM/ML performance — traces, evaluations, drift, embeddings, data quality, and hallucination/response quality (includes open-source Arize Phoenix).
features: LLM tracing and evaluation (Phoenix open-source + Arize AX)
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open-source (self-hostable); Arize AX offers a free tier with usage limits and custom Enterprise pricing for production scale.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing rigorous evaluation, drift detection, and large-scale ML + LLM monitoring.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, user feedback, and evaluation scores — open-source and framework-agnostic.
features: Cost and token tracking per trace
Evaluation and scoring (manual, model-based, user feedback)
tools.pricing: Free open-source self-hosted option; cloud Hobby tier free, Core/Pro plans starting around $29–$59/month, plus Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability stack with strong cost tracking and prompt management.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM and vector DB operations via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation — traces, token usage, latency, and costs exportable to any OTel-compatible backend.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Vendor-neutral export to any OTel backend (Datadog, Grafana, etc.)
Standardized semantic conventions for LLM telemetry
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs depend on the chosen backend/destination. Managed option available via Traceloop with free and paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that want vendor-neutral, standards-based LLM telemetry plugged into existing observability infrastructure.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (e.g., via Helicone or prompt caching) to avoid paying for identical LLM calls more than once.
Route tasks to the cheapest model that meets quality needs — use smaller or distilled models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Reduce token usage by trimming prompts, summarizing or truncating context, and limiting max output tokens; monitor per-trace costs to catch runaway spend early.
Set budgets, rate limits, and alerts on token/cost metrics so high-volume overages (which can add up to 5–10% of underlying LLM spend) are flagged before they escalate.
